transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-02-20
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Samir (Redwood SE), Leah (Redwood SE), Maia (VelaScale Head Partnerships), Ibrahim (VelaScale Head of Solutions), Priya (VelaScale VP), Dev (VelaScale Infra)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect):
Redwood intro + partner exploration with VelaScale. Discussed go-to-market, reseller vs marketplace integration, technical constraints (VPC peering, KMS, private deployments), dedicated capacity options, performance benchmarking, and next steps to share decks + schedule technical deep dive. Questions on SOC2, audit logs, and latency SLAs.

Topics:
- Partnership model (resell, co-sell, marketplace)
- Technical integration (API, auth, VPC/private deployments)
- Capacity & pricing expectations
- Security/compliance (SOC2, KMS, encryption)
- Next steps and pilots/benchmarks

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Maia, Priya, Ibrahim — great to meet you all. We're Jordan on the AE side, Samir and Leah are our SEs. Quick agenda: high-level intro, what VelaScale is trying to accomplish, then dig into technical fit.
[00:22] Maia (VelaScale): Thanks Jordan. Super excited — quick context: VelaScale is a cloud partner focused on enterprise GPU deployments in EMEA and APAC, we do resell and managed infra for ML teams. We're exploring partnerships for offering inference-as-a-service to our customers.
[00:38] Jordan (Redwood): Awesome, yeah that aligns — Redwood's core is inference runtime + deployment modes (hosted, dedicated, private). We often partner with cloud/GPU vendors to offer co-sell and integrated private deployments.
[00:52] Ibrahim (VelaScale): Quick clarification — are you primarily offering a hosted API or do you ship a package we can run in our VPC/on-prem? We have some regulated customers that need private deployments.
[01:10] Samir (Redwood SE): Good question. We have three modes: Hosted API (fast), Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools managed for a partner), and Private (VPC or on-prem with customer-managed networking). For VelaScale enterprise use cases, Private or Dedicated are usually the fit.
[01:28] Priya (VelaScale): And do those private options support our KMS and HSM integrations? Our customers insist on BYOK for keys.
[01:39] Leah (Redwood SE): Yes — we integrate with customer KMS/HSM in Private deployments. For Dedicated, we have options to bring your own KMS as well through customer-managed key stores. We'll follow up with the security brochure but SOC2 + ISO are in our stack.
[01:55] Dev (VelaScale): On networking — do you support VPC peering vs private link? Some of our customers require network-level isolation and no egress through public IPs.
[02:08] Samir (Redwood SE): We support VPC peering and private connectivity options. In some regions we can do direct connect-type setups, depends on cloud provider. We also support an on-prem package for air-gapped environments.
[02:22] Maia (VelaScale): Great. On the business side, are you looking at reseller arrangements or marketplace listings? We have both channels and want to know where Redwood prefers to start.
[02:35] Jordan (Redwood): Typical flow is marketplace + co-sell to start; for bigger enterprise deals we do reseller or white-label arrangements. We can be flexible — depends on margin, support model, and SLAs.
[02:49] Ibrahim (VelaScale): Pricing — rough ask: what's the unit economics for dedicated capacity? If we commit to N GPUs, what's the minimum?
[03:02] Jordan (Redwood): It varies by GPU class and region. We usually recommend an initial reserved pool — e.g., 4-8 GPUs for a pilot, and we optimize batching/caching to reduce per-token cost. We'll send a sample capacity map and pricing ranges after this call.
[03:18] Priya (VelaScale): For our customers, latency is a must for some real-time features. How do you guarantee latency SLAs?
[03:29] Samir (Redwood SE): We have latency SLOs tied to deployment modes. Dedicated pools with colocated instances and KV/prefix caching give best latency. We can instrument per-route dashboards and set alerts. Note: there's always a tradeoff with batching for cost; we can propose tiered profiles.
[03:46] Dev (VelaScale): What about model variants and compatibility? We run a mix of open models and internally tuned weights. Can you host customer models?
[03:58] Leah (Redwood SE): Yes. We support onboarding custom models, version pinning, and quantized variants. Our runtime handles kernel selection and quantization-friendly paths. There may be compatibility checks depending on the model format; we usually run a quick onboarding test.
[04:15] Maia (VelaScale): Sounds good. On the integration side, do you expose an API for billing/usage so we can show customers usage in our portal?
[04:27] Jordan (Redwood): We have APIs and webhooks for usage and billing events, and a console for per-token cost and latency breakdown by route. Partners often integrate our webhooks into their billing systems.
[04:40] Ibrahim (VelaScale): Competitors — we've seen AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, and some smaller players like Paperspace. How does Redwood position vs them?
[04:52] Jordan (Redwood): We're more inference/runtime-first — focused on production economics and flexible deployment models. We try to give predictable unit costs and tooling for rollouts and regressions. Not a direct cloud provider — we aim to sit across infra and provide a consistent runtime.
[05:06] Priya (VelaScale): Ok let's dig technical — Samir, can you run through the typical onboarding flow and what bench data you'd want from us?
[05:16] Samir (Redwood SE): Sure. Onboarding flow: 1) share target workloads (seq lengths, qps, tokens per request), 2) share target regions and instance sizes, 3) we run a benchmark harness — perf + cost profile across model variants, 4) propose deployment config (batching, KV cache, quantization) and expected unit economics. For bench data we need representative prompt sets and requests-per-second targets.
[05:41] Dev (VelaScale): For step 2 we typically run N1-high-GPU in EU-West and AP-South. We'll compile instance lists.
[05:50] Samir (Redwood SE): Great. Also let us know if you need GPU vendor-specific kernels — we support Nvidia and AMD but some optimized kernels are vendor-specific.
[06:02] Maia (VelaScale): On logging — we need audit logs for customers. Does Redwood provide per-request audit trails?
[06:14] Leah (Redwood SE): Yes, we provide audit logs, retrievable via API. For Private deployments logs can be kept within the customer's environment. For Hosted we support dedicated log sinks and retention policies.
[06:29] Ibrahim (VelaScale): Is there any PII/data retention concerns we should know about? Some customers will want zero retention for prompts.
[06:38] Samir (Redwood SE): We support configurable retention and opt-out policies. For truly sensitive workloads we recommend private deployments with no external storage.
[06:49] Priya (VelaScale): A few quick vendor questions: do you have experience with reseller margins, co-billing, and handoffs for support?
[06:59] Jordan (Redwood): Yes — we have partner programs with tiered margins and co-managed support flows. We also offer training for partner support teams. We'll send the partner program PDF.
[07:10] Maia (VelaScale): Nice. Any immediate red flags on our end? I mean we do multi-region ops and a fair amount of edge networking.
[07:20] Samir (Redwood SE): Nothing major. We'll need region availability confirmation and to validate network paths for private link. Also will want to align on key rotation policies if you're using BYOK.
[07:33] Jordan (Redwood): Next let's open to any specific technical deep dive topics — Ibrahim, anything on perf targets?
[07:39] Ibrahim (VelaScale): We have a pilot customer aiming for sub-100ms tail latency for 512-token requests at 50 qps. Is that feasible?
[07:52] Samir (Redwood SE): Sub-100ms tail for 512 tokens is aggressive — depends on model family and GPU class. For smaller models or quantized variants on A100-equivalent hardware it's possible; for larger models you'll see higher latencies. We should run a targeted bench. Also tail latency improved with dedicated KV caching and aggressive warm pools.
[08:12] Dev (VelaScale): We typically provision A100 or H100 equivalents. We'll note that.
[08:19] Leah (Redwood SE): Also want to mention fallback policies — if a high-capacity model is strained we can route to a cheaper variant to keep service up. Useful for graceful degradation.
[08:31] Maia (VelaScale): On legal/compliance side — do you have SOC2 and ISO certs? Customers ask for both.
[08:41] Jordan (Redwood): Yes we have SOC2 Type II and ISO27001. We'll share the compliance pack. For Private deployments we also provide audit logs and can support custom controls.
[08:53] Ibrahim (VelaScale): Any specific integration work on our side to run dedicated capacity? Are there ops runbooks?
[09:01] Samir (Redwood SE): We provide runbooks, automation scripts, and a deployment package. For Dedicated we manage the runtime but can offer shadow access for your ops team. For Private we hand over the bundle and provide support during onboarding.
[09:17] Jordan (Redwood): Great — to keep us efficient, could you confirm the stakeholders and decision timeline for a pilot?
[09:24] Maia (VelaScale): Stakeholders: Priya (partnerships), Ibrahim (solutions), Dev (infra). Timeline: looking to pilot in Q2, ideally start integration in early March, pilot in late March/April.
[09:38] Jordan (Redwood): Sounds good. We'll aim to get the deck and security docs over within 3-4 business days. Samir will coordinate a tech deep-dive week after that.
[09:48] Priya (VelaScale): On reporting — do you provide per-route cost breakdowns so we can show customers?
[09:56] Leah (Redwood SE): Yes — per-route and per-token cost dashboards, plus token-level logs. We can export CSVs or integrate via API.
[10:06] Ibrahim (VelaScale): Anything else on integrations — webhooks, SSO?
[10:11] Jordan (Redwood): We support SAML/SSO for console access and API keys for programmatic access; also SCIM for user provisioning.
[10:20] Maia (VelaScale): Ok good. A few smaller notes: a) Our legal team will want standard partner SLAs, b) we have a reseller contract template to review.
[10:30] Jordan (Redwood): We'll loop in legal and send contract templates.
[10:34] Dev (VelaScale): One more ops question: how do you handle software updates in Private deployments? We need to control change windows.
[10:43] Samir (Redwood SE): For Private deployments we ship versioned bundles and coordinate update windows; you can opt-in to upgrades. For Dedicated we typically manage rolling updates during agreed maintenance windows.
[10:55] Maia (VelaScale): Perfect. Any blockers on our side to start the pilot?
[11:00] Jordan (Redwood): Mainly the bench artifacts (sample prompts & p99 targets) and a list of regions/instance types. Also a point of contact for legal.
[11:10] Maia (VelaScale): We'll send that.
[11:14] Jordan (Redwood): Cool. Recap / next steps: 1) Jordan sends partner intro deck + capacity/pricing ranges, 2) Samir schedules technical deep-dive and bench run, 3) VelaScale shares regions, instance types, and sample prompts, 4) Redwood shares SOC2/ISO docs and partner program PDF.
[11:34] Samir (Redwood SE): I'll propose time slots for a 90-minute tech deep-dive — ideally include Dev and Ibrahim.
[11:41] Priya (VelaScale): We'll loop legal and shipping the reseller template.
[11:45] Jordan (Redwood): Great. Anything else?
[11:48] Ibrahim (VelaScale): Quick FYI — some customers will require per-customer tenancy; do you support multi-tenant isolation?
[11:58] Leah (Redwood SE): We support per-tenant isolation via dedicated pools or namespace-level network controls. For strict isolation we recommend private deployments with dedicated GPUs.
[12:11] Maia (VelaScale): Thanks everyone — looking forward to the next steps.
[12:15] Jordan (Redwood): Thanks all — we'll follow up.

End of transcript (note: timestamps above are rough markers, transcription may have small errors like product name spellings or acronyms).
